abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a novel theoretical framework that fundamentally reconceptualizes the relationship between neural synchrony and cognitive information processing in connectionist systems. Moving beyond traditional rate-based neural coding assumptions, we propose a unified temporal coding paradigm that integrates discrete symbolic representations with continuous neural dynamics through phase-amplitude coupling mechanisms. Our theoretical analysis demonstrates that this hybrid encoding scheme resolves long-standing limitations in connectionist modeling regarding binding problems and dynamic context maintenance. By reformulating learning algorithms within this framework, we establish new convergence bounds that show significant improvements over standard gradient-based methods, particularly for temporally structured data. The mathematical formalism reveals how parallel distributed processing can simultaneously achieve compositional representation and robust temporal reasoning without requiring dedicated binding units. We term this approach Temporal Binding Neural Networks (TBNN), and prove its theoretical properties including universal approximation under biologically plausible constraints. This work challenges the dominant deep learning paradigm by demonstrating that architectures incorporating explicit temporal dynamics can achieve superior generalization on cognitive modeling tasks while maintaining interpretability. Our contribution establishes theoretical foundations for next-generation brain-inspired computing systems that bridge symbolic and neural approaches to artificial intelligence.

We present a rigorous theoretical analysis of attention mechanisms within recurrent neural networks that substantially extends existing understanding of their learning dynamics. While attention has demonstrated empirical success in sequence modeling, its theoretical role in parallel distributed processing remains poorly understood. This paper develops a comprehensive mathematical framework characterizing how attention-weighted feedback connections modulate neural dynamics during gradient-based learning. We prove that incorporating structured attention patterns improves the conditioning number of the loss landscape, leading to accelerated convergence rates that scale logarithmically with sequence length—addressing a fundamental limitation of vanilla RNNs. Our analysis reveals that attention acts as a learned gating mechanism that implements adaptive memory compression, providing theoretical justification for its effectiveness in computational neuroscience applications modeling working memory. We further derive generalization bounds that demonstrate attention-equipped networks achieve tighter bounds on hypothesis complexity compared to baseline architectures. Importantly, our theoretical insights translate into concrete algorithmic improvements: we propose Modified Attention Constraints (MAC) that can be incorporated into existing deep learning frameworks with minimal computational overhead. Experiments on cognitive modeling tasks validate our theoretical predictions, showing 23% improvement in long-range dependency tasks and more robust continual learning behavior.

We introduce NeuroCognitive Architecture (NCA), a novel brain-inspired computing system that implements the first complete computational model integrating working memory, episodic memory, and procedural learning within a unified neural substrate. Unlike existing modular approaches that simulate cognitive functions through disconnected components, NCA employs a cortical column simulation featuring thousands of spiking neurons connected through biologically-plausible synaptic plasticity rules. The architecture introduces Hierarchical Predictive Coding modules that enable real-time learning through predictive error minimization across multiple temporal scales. Our system implements a groundbreaking integration of deep learning capabilities with cognitive modeling requirements, including automatic goal representation, flexible behavior composition, and robust transfer learning. We demonstrate NCA's capabilities through comprehensive evaluation on the HORNE benchmark suite, showing human-level performance on complex tasks requiring planning and analogical reasoning while maintaining online learning from streaming data. The system achieves this through a novel attention-gated memory mechanism that dynamically routes information between short-term and long-term storage based on task relevance. Importantly, NCA operates with unprecedented energy efficiency, consuming three orders of magnitude less power than comparable deep learning systems performing equivalent cognitive tasks. This work establishes a new paradigm for intelligent systems development that bridges computational neuroscience and machine learning.

This paper presents Synaptic Cascade Networks (SCN), an advanced neural network architecture that substantially improves upon existing deep learning systems for temporal sequence processing. SCN introduces a novel multi-timescale memory integration mechanism that dynamically allocates computational resources based on input volatility, addressing the well-known problem of catastrophic forgetting in sequential learning tasks. Our system extends traditional LSTM architectures by incorporating differentiable plastic synapses that automatically adjust their learning rates based on local error signals, achieving superior performance on benchmarks including sequential MNIST, permuted tasks, and real-world financial prediction datasets. The architectural innovations include: (1) a Cascade Memory Buffer enabling efficient rehearsal of rare events without external storage, (2) Adaptive Forget Gates that respond to concept drift in non-stationary environments, and (3) a novel loss function combining temporal difference learning with supervised objectives. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SCN achieves state-of-the-art results across twelve benchmark datasets, with relative improvements of 15-40% over previous best methods. Notably, the system maintains its performance advantages even when trained on resource-constrained edge devices, requiring 67% fewer parameters than competing approaches. The computational analysis confirms that SCN's complexity scales linearly with sequence length, making it practical for real-time applications in computational neuroscience and industrial monitoring. We provide open-source implementation to facilitate reproducible research.
